name: Edificio España

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/49031978 (centroid of the outline; long axis at 145.2°, the Plaza de España façade faces 235.2°)

rights.note: Julián Otamendi designed the building and its Baroque main portal; his brother José María Otamendi, engineer, calculated the concrete structure (Compañía Inmobiliaria Metropolitana, 1948–1953). Façades restored 2005–2010 (Rubio & Álvarez-Sala); refurbished as a hotel 2017–2019 (rooftop terrace with glazed pavilions).

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q649426_edificio_espana.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. The massing is the OpenStreetMap building:part pieces extruded to their heights (three balcony overhangs with min_level left out). OSM pieces without a height get one from the floor grid counted on a perspective-corrected photo: granite base 0–9 m (shop floor and mezzanine), floors of 3.55 m to the slab cornice at 70 m and its attic at 73.8 m, upper tower floors of 3.7 m, its glazed attic gallery and balustrade at about 98.5 m, the lantern with its round oculus to 105.5 m and the flagpole to the quoted 117 m. The OSM heights 107 (upper tower) and 117 (lantern) were not used as such: counted floors give a lower roof, and 117 m is reached only with the mast — the vertical split of the top 20 m is uncertain (±5 m). Brick panels (front centre, wing fronts, the four sides of the upper tower) as seen on the photos; the side and back façades are shown in white stone with the same window grid, which is a simplification (their real pattern was not checked). Windows are dark quads on a 3.2 m grid aligned across the pieces; the Baroque portal, cornices, balustrades and pinnacles are stylised; the curved balconies of the wing corners and the rooftop pool are not modelled. The central light well of the upper tower and the five back courtyards follow OSM.
